subject: Retention cadence alignment and emergency purge guardrails — TheraBridge DPA
messages:
From: Diane Khan <diane.khan@therabridge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@therabridge.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: retention windows + emergency purge carveouts (TheraBridge)

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and security asked me to confirm a few items so we can finish the DPA addendum:

1) Our retention policy requires user activity logs and conversational transcripts be retained for 540 days, but backups of underlying storage are allowed to have a longer lifecycle (up to 720 days) provided there is a documented purge schedule.
2) If Redwood uses subprocessors with cross-border transfers, we need the subprocessors identified and the transfer mechanism called out (SCCs or adequacy).
3) We need an emergency purge procedure that can be triggered by TheraBridge security for specific accounts (e.g., suspected account compromise) with an SLA for execution and evidence of completion.

Can you point to where these are documented or share a proposed schedule for the backup purge and log-retention carveouts?

Also attaching a draft table of retention buckets — please review.

Best,
Diane
Head of Legal, TheraBridge

Subject: Re: Initial: retention windows + emergency purge carveouts (TheraBridge)

Hi Diane —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers and next steps below; I'll loop in Ops for the purge SLA details.

- Retention buckets: Redwood application-level logs and transcripts default to 540 days for customer-configurable retention. We keep immutable daily snapshots (backups) for up to 720 days in the default configuration; these are considered disaster-recovery artifacts and are not served to product flows. Customers can request shorter backup retention via their contract.

- Subprocessors & transfers: We publish our subprocessor roster and transfer mechanisms in the DPA addendum; we support SCCs and use regionally partitioned storage for EU customers by default. If you need named subprocessor confirmation (by service type), we can provide a sealed list for legal review.

- Emergency purge: We have an emergency purge playbook that supports a customer-initiated purge request. Typical flow: 1) formal request via security contact + signed attest; 2) Ops schedules a targeted purge of application-layer data within 24 hours (where feasible) and backup purge within 5 business days (depending on snapshot retention windows and replication). We capture purge evidence (audit log, tombstone ids) and deliver a signed report.

I'll follow up with Marcus from Ops on the exact timeline for backup deletion and whether we can accelerate to 48–72 hours for high-severity incidents.

Action: I'll upload the standard DPA addendum and the purge playbook excerpts to Drive and share a link by EOD.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial: retention windows + emergency purge carveouts (TheraBridge)

Diane / Mina —

Operational clarification from Infra/Storage:
- Backups live on a 3-tier snapshot schedule: daily (30 days hot window), weekly (90 days), monthly (remainder up to configured max). The default max is 720 days.
- For customer-targeted emergency purge we can tombstone application-layer objects within 24 hours. Backup reconciliation is trickier: if a target object is included in an immutable snapshot, we need to rewrite/replicate snapshot manifests to exclude the objects, which currently takes up to 5 business days in our standard runbook.
- For TheraBridge (enterprise customer) we can offer an accelerated backup purge SLA (48–72 hours) as a contract amendment if you commit to a Dedicated capacity pool or a Private deployment.

I'll attach the purge-runbook excerpt.

Marcus
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Marcus — that's helpful. A few follow-ups from security/legal:

1) We need the purge evidence format to include: timestamped audit entries, object ids removed, and the hash of the manifest pre/post purge.
2) For cross-border subprocessors: can Redwood provide the list of subprocessors that handle backups specifically (not general SAAS vendors)? We need to know which parties could have snapshot access.
3) If TheraBridge signs an amendment for an accelerated 72-hour backup purge SLA, we'd like an exception clause for EU data that requires a local copy verification step before final deletion (because of our regulatory obligations).

Can you confirm whether those items can be included in the addendum? We're hoping to finalize by next Tuesday.

Best,
Diane
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Diane Khan <diane.khan@therabridge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Mar 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: retention windows + emergency purge carveouts (TheraBridge)

Diane —

We're aligned on the key asks and can include them in the addendum. Summary of commitments we will draft into the DPA addendum and run by Legal:

- Retention: application logs/transcripts default 540 days; backups default 720 days; customer may request shorter backup retention via amendment.
- Emergency purge SLA: application-layer purge evidence delivered within 24 hours; backup manifest rewrite and confirmed deletion delivered within 72 business hours under accelerated SLA (48–72 hrs where Dedicated/Private deployment purchased). Evidence package will include timestamped audit logs, removed object ids, and pre/post manifest hashes (or signed manifest digest).
- Subprocessors: we will include a sub-list limited to backup/replication vendors and confirm transfer mechanisms (SCCs/adequacy). For TheraBridge we will provide a sealed subprocessor report and a designated point of contact in Legal to review.
- EU verification step: we can add a clause requiring local copy verification for EU-designated data before final deletion; this will add a coordination step but we'll commit to documenting timelines in the addendum.

Next steps: I'll share the redline of the DPA addendum and the purge-runbook excerpt in the Drive link (see doc link) and propose a short review call on Wed 3/29 to finalize language.

If that works, please accept the DocuSign envelope that I'll send after legal-internal review.

Thanks,
Mina
